body.statement: Does there exist a game in \(\mathcal G_p\) with \(p=2\), rational vertices of \(H\), rational entries of \(\Sigma\), rational endpoint intercepts and normals, and a finite prior \(\pi\in\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\) having rational support points, rational masses, and unequal total masses on the two endpoint signs, such that the finite curved-score certificate holds for \(\delta_{\pi}\); or are these requirements impossible in two dimensions? An affirmative certificate must instantiate \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{noidx}}\): give a rational \(q\), finite rational box partitions, outward-rounded interval enclosures, and analytic Gaussian-tail bounds proving \(R(\delta_{\pi})\le q\le b(\pi)\). It must also enclose \(B_{\pi}\), its first two derivatives, and \(\mathcal K_{\pi}\) on a rational box meeting a nondegenerate arc \(\Gamma\subset\mathcal Z_{\pi}\), with strictly positive rational lower bounds on the score-gradient norm and on \( |\mathcal K_{\pi}|\), and certify \(B_{\pi}\not\equiv0\). The conclusion \(R(\delta_{\pi})=b(\pi)=v=q\), uniqueness almost everywhere, and \(\mathcal D^{\star}\cap\mathcal D_1=\varnothing\) must then follow through \(\mathrm{thm:curved-score-no-index-certificate}\), rather than being assumed.
body.justification: This remains the early kill test for the no-one-index branch. The explicit rational attempt shows that unbalanced masses and a curved Gaussian-mixture boundary are easy to obtain separately, but exact least-favorability fails and cannot be repaired by numerical precision alone.
body.gap: The unresolved step is an exact non-collinear rational equalizer: rational saddle value and endpoint data force rational Gaussian decision probabilities at every charged support point, while no verified source or frozen record supplies the required symmetry, interval certificate, or impossibility theorem.
body.consumer: A successful certificate would prove that genuinely multivariate reporting is sometimes unavoidable; a general impossibility theorem would sharply simplify the classification program. The failed square candidate prevents software from mistaking a curved approximate Bayes boundary for exact minimax closure.

obligation.what_is_open: An affirmative rational certificate remains open.  Concretely, one must exhibit a finite signed Gaussian mixture with non-collinear rational support and rational effective weights whose Bayes decision probabilities at every charged support point equal the rational numbers forced by complementary slackness, and then certify the continuum of endpoint risks and a curved regular score-zero arc.  Alternatively, one must prove that no such rational mixture can occur in dimension two.
obligation.obstruction:
The exact rational requirements impose an arithmetic constraint that interval approximation cannot replace.  Nontrivial sign ambiguity implies \(v>0\).  If a rational certificate had value \(q=v\), then at every positively charged state \((h,+)\) or \((h,-)\), respectively,
\[
 q_{\delta_\pi}(h)=1-\frac{q}{c_+(h)}
 \quad\hbox{or}\quad
 q_{\delta_\pi}(h)=\frac{q}{c_-(h)}.
\]
Because rational affine endpoint data evaluated at rational \(h\) give rational nonzero \(c_+(h)\) and \(c_-(h)\), every displayed Gaussian decision probability must be exactly rational.  The frozen core supplies neither a candidate satisfying these equalities nor a symbolic symmetry that proves them.  A positive-width outward-rounded enclosure can prove a strict inequality, but it cannot by itself prove equality of an analytic Gaussian probability to a prescribed rational number.  Assuming these equalities, or replacing the requested rational support by roots of analytic equations, would assume the crux or violate the target.
obligation.attempted:
The prior round reduced the implication from a completed certificate to \(\mathrm{thm:curved-score-no-index-certificate}\).  This round tested the most economical rational unbalanced construction exactly.  Its complete rational primitive table is
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
\text{object}&\text{rational data}\\ \hline
p&2\\
H&\operatorname{conv}\{(-2,-2),(2,-2),(2,2),(-2,2)\}=[-2,2]^2\\
\Sigma&\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\\
J_-&\{1\},\quad a_1^-=-1,\quad b_1^-=(0,0)^\top\\
J_+&\{1\},\quad a_1^+=3/4,\quad b_1^+=(0,0)^\top
\end{array}
\]
and the complete prior table is
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
h&\text{endpoint sign}&\pi\text{-mass}\\ \hline
(1,0)&+&1/3\\
(-1,0)&+&1/3\\
(0,1)&-&1/6\\
(0,-1)&-&1/6
\end{array}.
\]
Thus \(\ell(h)=-1\) and \(u(h)=3/4\).  All support points lie in \(\operatorname{ri}(H)\), all displayed data are rational, and the endpoint-sign masses are \(2/3\) and \(1/3\).  The game satisfies every member condition of \(\mathcal G_2\): the square is a compact full-dimensional polytope, \(I_2\) is positive definite, \(-1<3/4\), and the interval strictly straddles zero at every \(h\).

Writing \(\varphi=\varphi_{I_2}\), direct completion of squares gives
\[
 A_{\pi,+}(z)=\frac12 e^{-1/2}\varphi(z)\cosh z_1,
 \qquad
 A_{\pi,-}(z)=\frac13 e^{-1/2}\varphi(z)\cosh z_2,
\]
and hence
\[
 B_\pi(z)=e^{-1/2}\varphi(z)
 \left(\frac12\cosh z_1-\frac13\cosh z_2\right).
\]
Thus its Bayes rule has the genuinely non-halfspace boundary
\(3\cosh z_1=2\cosh z_2\).  This candidate nevertheless fails exact saddle closure for a symbolic reason.  Since \(\min(A_{\pi,+},A_{\pi,-})\leq A_{\pi,-}\),
\[
 b(\pi)\leq\int_{\mathbb R^2}A_{\pi,-}(z)\,dz=\frac13.
\]
At \(h=0\), any rule with \(x=q_\delta(0)\) has worst signed risk at least
\[
 \max\left\{\frac34(1-x),x\right\}\geq\frac37.
\]
Consequently \(v\geq3/7>1/3\geq b(\pi)\), so this rational unbalanced curved-score prior is not least favorable and cannot be face-complete.  It is therefore an explicit witness attempt, not a substitute conditional theorem.

Two exact structural checks further delimit the search.  First, if \(h_0\) is the sign-ambiguity point and \(x=q_\delta(h_0)\), then
\[
 \max\{u(h_0)(1-x),[-\ell(h_0)]x\}
 \geq\frac{u(h_0)[-\ell(h_0)]}{u(h_0)-\ell(h_0)}>0,
\]
which proves \(v>0\).  Second, if all support points having nonzero net signed mixture coefficient lie on an affine line \(\bar h+\mathbb R d\), factoring the positive density \(\varphi_\Sigma(z-\bar h)\) from \(B_\pi\) shows that its sign is a function only of \(d^\top\Sigma^{-1}z\).  Its Bayes rule is then one-index.  Hence a curved certificate requires non-collinear effective support; the usual common-reflection device that forces probability \(1/2\) along a single line cannot settle this target.
obligation.partial_result:
The strongest closed result is an exact obstruction plus an explicit failed rational candidate.  In any requested certificate, nontrivial sign ambiguity makes \(q=v>0\), complementary slackness makes every charged support risk equal \(q\), and rational primitives therefore force every charged Gaussian treatment probability to be rational through
\(q_{\delta_\pi}(h)=1-q/c_+(h)\) or \(q_{\delta_\pi}(h)=q/c_-(h)\).  Effective support confined to an affine line necessarily gives a one-index Bayes rule, so a successful witness must solve these rational-probability equalities on a non-collinear rational support.  The displayed square example is fully rational, has unequal endpoint-sign masses and the curved analytic boundary \(3\cosh z_1=2\cosh z_2\), but it is ruled out exactly by \(b(\pi)\leq1/3<3/7\leq v\).  No remaining record in the supplied immutable core provides the non-collinear rational equalizer, rational partition, truncation box, directed enclosures, or tail receipts needed to pass from this obstruction to an affirmative certificate or a general impossibility theorem.
